questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature and possibilities of outdoor recreation in the host country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a few email correspondences with the Go Global office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Several housing opportunities, I chose to prioritize the shared unit-options.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Shared housing had kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Most people living in Fairview lived with other exchange students. The kitchens are not equipped, which mean spending a good amount of money on utensils, bedding etc when arriving (at least in the fall semester)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy to just fill out the survey sent out by UBC.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UBC sends out an email with a link to the registration survey, and you can just fill it out with any courses from the course catalogue.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The study counselling Go Global could help with course choices.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fairly successful and it was easy to change courses via email afterwards.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the first 2 weeks of classes to talk to fellow students and figure out if the profs in your courses are good - if not, switch to other courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The continuous evaluation makes studying more stressful, and there are a lot of small assignments to do that count for the final grade. Some profs did not seem very interested in teaching, while other were very good teachers.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I mostly took 300 level courses, which weren't too challenging, but pretty suitable as I took 4 courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: at UCPH, there is not much continuous evaluation, which makes students much less stressed, whereas students in general were quite stressed at UBC.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GEOS270 Geographic Information Science
UFOR316 Trees and Shrubs in Landscape
CHEM301 Aqueous Environmental Chemistry
FRE374 Land and Resource Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would mostly recommend GEOS270 and UFOR316. Both June Skeeter and Athena McKnown were amazing profs and topics were super interesting and useful! CHEM301 was interesting, but not taught as well. FRE374 was a very difficult and poorly taught course - don't take it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Phone bills were quite expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than expected - I would recommend going to Persia Foods, which was the cheapest. Travel costs (included in personal spendings) to visit different places within BC where more than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of opportunities!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Anything you could imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The varsity outdoor club, the UBC yoga club, sprouts (student run café), the aviary

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on the VOC trips, go on hikes and see the mountains.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: yes

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: get to know people in your classes - have a cup of coffee after class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: in general students are younger than the typical danish university student, so it takes a little adjustment

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the love for the outdoors and possibilities to go to the mountains.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: don't focus too much on studying. try to go other places than vancouver to see different parts of Canada.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: many other exchange students are at UBC for a full year.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Many great hiking trips and other outdoor activities.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The age difference to other students. Many students socialized partying and drinking, so if you're not wanting to do that every weekend, be prepared to find friends in other ways.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
